----DISCLAIMER: I ONLY HAVE THE PRODUCT IN MY POSSESSION ON THIS VIDEO BECAUSE I HAD THE VENDOR SHIP IT TO ME FIRST SO I CAN MAKE CONTENT. During dropshipping you usually won't physically touch the product that you are selling. ---- •First I listed my products online on a shopify website. Before doing this you'll need to develop a pricelist to make sure you are receiving your desired profit after buying the product from the vendor. Don't have a reliable dropshipping vendor? Check out my personal vendors on my website!  • For my website product pictures, I used pictures online from google and edited my logo into the picture until I was able to have an actual photoshoot for my products. (WHEN DOING THIS MAKE SURE YOU FIND PICTURES THAT DOESN'T HAVE ANOTHER COMPANY'S LOGO VISIBLE! THIS IS FOR COPYRIGHT REASONS)  •Since you won't have the product on hand yet, I recommend buying one sample of the product to be able to advertise so customers can see it is in your possession. For example, I bought one 18" bundle and advertised that in many videos until I received my first order. I also bought a wig from my vendor and installed it in a video to promote that to customers as well.  •ONCE YOU RECEIVE YOUR FIRST ORDER, HAVE THE VENDOR SHIP IT TO YOU FIRST SO YOU CAN BE ABLE TO CREATE CONTENT THEN YOU WILL SHIP IT BACK OUT TO YOUR CUSTOMER. (When shipping back out you will lose a little profit but no more than $15-$20) This is very important because it allows you to keep building a portfolio of your product & brand. Most customers don't order a product unless they see it is being advertised frequently and correctly.  •You will have to manually contact your vendor after receiving each order. Shopify does not automatically alert them. (I usually use whatsapp when contacting my vendors) •When creating content I used natural sunlight until I was able to purchase my 18" ring light. This is how dropshipping actually works: First, you create your online store. You can do this with Shopify for $1/month. I also recommend connecting it to pagepilot.ai so you can just have AI design the store for you. Next, you sign up for Zendrop and link it to Shopify. Zendrop is your supplier. Essentially, they stock the product you're selling on your store. Then, when somebody buys the product on your store, Zendrop is notified, and they package up the product and ship it to your customer. You don't have to touch the product once. This way, you don't have to spend thousands buying a bunch of inventory. You only pay Zendrop once the customer has paid you first. #ecom #entrepreneur #business #shopify #onlinebusiness
